name: Braintree
summary: PayPal's API-oriented payment platform for cards, PayPal, wallets, vaulting, recurring billing, and enterprise checkout.

pricing.headline: US standard card and wallet pricing is 2.89% + $0.29, with additional international and non-USD fees.
pricing.assumptions: US standard domestic card or third-party wallet. Approval is required and regional rates differ.

sellerCoverage: Availability and onboarding are market-specific and subject to PayPal application and approval.
buyerCoverage: Global card and PayPal acceptance depends on merchant location, currency, and enabled methods.
products: Broad eligible ecommerce and subscription businesses subject to PayPal policies and underwriting.

features.checkout: Drop-in UI, hosted fields, GraphQL and SDK integrations.
features.invoicing: Not primarily positioned as an invoicing suite; pair with merchant billing workflows as needed.
features.paymentMethods: Cards, PayPal, Venmo where eligible, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and regional methods.
features.payouts: Merchant settlement under the applicable Braintree and PayPal account terms.

responsibilities.note: Braintree provides payment services; the business sells the product.
Optional protection tools and dispute workflows exist, with eligibility and fees.
The merchant supports fulfillment, billing questions, and products.

strengths: PayPal and card acceptance in one developer platform
limitations: The merchant still owns tax and support operations
avoidIf: You want the provider to become legal seller
